metadata.title: Metrics Board Update
metadata.subject: Neutral board-style update for metrics, progress, risk, and asks
metadata.author: PresentationKit

processFlow.title: How the update earns confidence
processFlow.subtitle: A board update connects metric movement, interpretation, action, risk, and asks.
processFlow.caption: Metrics need interpretation before they become governance.

footprint.title: Update sections
footprint.subtitle: Keep the audience oriented across performance, progress, risk, and decisions.
footprint.caption: The structure keeps the discussion actionable.

architecture.title: Metrics evidence model
architecture.subtitle: Signals are paired with interpretation, caveats, actions, and governance asks.

slides.label: 1 / update context
slides.title: A board update should make decisions easier
slides.headline: The best update turns metrics into interpretation, action, and explicit asks.
slides.supportingLine: Open with the structure that connects measurement to governance decisions.
slides.speakerNotes: Set up the update as a decision-support artifact, not a dashboard screenshot.

slides.label: 2 / update proof
slides.title: Metrics become useful when caveats and actions are visible
slides.headline: The update separates performance signals from interpretation and decisions.
slides.supportingLine: Use proof artifacts to show trend, delivery, risk, and the support requested from the audience.
slides.guardrailLine: Guardrails: label proxy metrics; show trend not noise; separate update from ask.
slides.speakerNotes: Make the board-level ask clear and grounded in the metric narrative.

slides.label: 3 / update ambition
slides.title: The dream: governance conversations focus on the right decisions
slides.headline: A concise update helps leaders spend time on trade-offs, risks, and support.
slides.closingLine: Use metrics to focus the conversation, not to hide the decisions.
slides.speakerNotes: Close by reinforcing the intended decision or support needed after the update.
